docs.summary: Draws the effects of the volumes the camera listens to and of its base profile.
The camera's own effects, under every volume: an asset, or a profile embedded in the scene.
The layers of the volumes the camera listens to.
Where local volumes are measured from, the camera itself when empty.
Renders into 16 bit float colour, which a [`Tonemapping`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Rendering.Tonemapping) volume component maps to the display. Off renders into 8 bit sRGB, where light above 1 clips.
Half the height of the orthographic view, in world units, so the view spans twice this from top to bottom and as much across as the target's aspect calls for.
The farthest distance the camera draws and effects such as fog and shadows reach.
The part of the target the camera draws into, as x, y, width and height from 0 to 1, y down from the top.
Cameras draw lowest depth first, each over the ones before.

The camera shown on top: the enabled camera with the highest [`Depth`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Camera~Depth) in the current scene that draws to the screen. Cameras drawing into a render texture, cameras stacked over others and editor helper cameras are never main. Found once per frame, null when there is none.
The render texture asset this camera draws into. None means it draws wherever the render it takes part in is going: the window in a player, the Game View or scene view texture in the editor.
Resolution the camera renders at against its target, presented scaled to fit.

The headset eyes this camera renders while XR is running. A perspective camera with no [`Target`](#api~Prowl.Motion.Target) renders both eyes from its transform, which stands for the head, into the headset.
The id of this camera's view, which keys Graphite's state for it such as temporal history.
